evidence.note: NOT DELIVERED, and the frozen contract is FALSE as shipped — stated here because the field cannot be edited and must not be quietly left standing. CHK-003's userSees says 'a rejection naming CHK-001 and one naming CHK-002 digest differently'. Against the shipped code that exact pair is a MUST-STILL-COLLAPSE case. The item asked for something that is not achievable from message text alone, and that is proven rather than estimated: evidence.output is interpolated verbatim into a story_advance DONE rejection at core/machine.ts:1190, so a third-party TAP label such as bug-2 is the SAME STRING as a real artifact ordinal, and any rule recognising one recognises the other. Eight successive recognition rules were each broken by cross-host review on a different shape before the eighth showed they were eight measurements of one impossibility. Consistent with every exclusion decision on this story, the tie breaks toward collapse because over-recognising is the dangerous direction for a brake. The withdrawal is machine-checked, not merely described: 'must-still-collapse checklist-ordinal' and 'unfixed-bug-ordinal' [guard: digit-rule-collapse] assert the OPPOSITE of this item, beside 'embedded-test-output-third-party-label' built from the reported pair. The operator confirmed the scope shrinkage and scope-shrinkage-decision.json records CHK-003 as removed with this reasoning.

evidence.note: NOT DELIVERED, cited against the case that actually tests it. This intent asked that a story id such as B-bf52, whose digits attach to an identifier, survive normalization so rejections naming different stories are not conflated. The case that tests exactly that is 'must-still-collapse bcc54-story-id-digits [guard: digit-rule-collapse]', which digests b-1234 and b-5678 to one key and so asserts the OPPOSITE of the intent — confirming the not-delivered verdict directly. An earlier version of this note cited 'review-loop-ordinal' and 'init-check-issue-ordinal' instead; those hold the story id CONSTANT and vary only a bookkeeping suffix, so they proved nothing about this intent. The verdict was right and the citation was wrong, which is the same defect class as F-049 and F-050 on this story. The underlying reason is the one recorded for CHK-003 throughout: a bare ordinal in a rejection is textually identical to a third-party label, so recognising story ids is not achievable from message text alone, and for a brake the tie breaks toward collapse.
